name: Iglesia vaginal mesh trial
question: Does adding vaginal polypropylene mesh to colpopexy improve anatomic success over traditional vaginal repair without mesh for stage 2–4 prolapse?

design.population: Women with POP-Q stage 2–4 pelvic organ prolapse undergoing vaginal repair.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind superiority randomized trial; early efficacy analyses grouped one mesh-assigned crossover with the 33 no-mesh operations
design.locator: Full text, Iglesia 2010, Methods, pp 294–297; Gutman 2013, Fig. 1, p 774

verdictNote: No demonstrated cure advantage; enrollment stopped after 5/32 mesh exposures.
takeaway: After one mesh-assigned crossover, early outcomes were analyzed by operation (32 mesh, 33 no mesh). No objective or subjective cure advantage was demonstrated; five mesh recipients had exposure (15.6%), exceeding the stopping threshold. Three-year composite cure was 8/23 versus 8/21 (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.42–1.99).

reports.label: Three-month primary report
reports.citation: Iglesia CB, Sokol AI, Sokol ER, et al. "Vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2010;116(2 Pt 1):293-303. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3181e7d7f8
reports.followUp: Three-month primary assessment; median 9.7 months at early stopping (range 2.4–26.7)

results.measure: Overall POP-Q stage 1 or lower; primary endpoint specified at 3 months, with anatomic outcomes tabulated at median 9.7 months
results.note: Early analysis grouped the one mesh-assigned crossover with no-mesh operations; additional prolapse surgery or pessary use counted as failure.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 296; Table 3, p 300

results.measure: Overall POP-Q stage 2 or higher recurrence at median 9.7 months
results.note: The abstract prints 70.4% for the no-mesh arm; the Results text and denominator give 72.7%. Of 43 recurrences, 33 remained at or above the hymen.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 297; Table 3, p 300

results.note: Abstract and Results give percentages but no arm-specific respondent denominators for this symptom item.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 293; Table 3, p 300

harms.label: Vaginal mesh exposure
harms.note: The 15% prespecified exposure threshold stopped enrollment; three exposures required operating-room excision, one resolved after office trimming and estrogen, and one persisted asymptomatically.

harms.label: Cystotomy
harms.note: One cystotomy occurred during dissection and one during trocar insertion; both were repaired.

harms.label: Blood transfusion
harms.note: Postoperative transfusion in a mesh recipient who also underwent hysterectomy.

harms.label: Early reoperation for prolapse, exposure or another indication
harms.note: P=.048; Table 3 counts five operations in four mesh recipients.

harms.label: Major infection requiring postoperative antibiotics
harms.note: No major infection requiring postoperative antibiotics or mesh infection was reported; two-week UTI counts were not given.

delivery.label: Mesh placement
delivery.value: Of 32 mesh operations, 24 used anterior Prolift and eight total Prolift; multi-armed polypropylene mesh traversed transobturator and ischiorectal trocar paths, was attached to the apex with 2-0 polydioxanone, and trimmed to vaginal caliber.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 296; Table 2, p 299

delivery.label: Native-tissue operation
delivery.value: Among 33 no-mesh operations, 29 used uterosacral, three sacrospinous and one iliococcygeus suspension; all included anterior colporrhaphy.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 296; Table 2, p 299

delivery.label: Treatment crossover and analysis set
delivery.value: One of 33 women randomized to mesh received no mesh because vaginal caliber was inadequate; the 2010 and 2012 reports analyzed her with the 33 no-mesh operations rather than by intention to treat.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 294; Gutman 2013, Methods, p 772

reports.label: One-year outcomes
reports.citation: Sokol AI, Iglesia CB, Kudish BI, et al. "One-year objective and functional outcomes of a randomized clinical trial of vaginal mesh for prolapse." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2012;206(1):86.e1-9. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2011.08.003
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; 60/65 (92.3%) had a POP-Q evaluation at 12 months (5 mesh patients censored)

results.measure: Overall POP-Q stage 1 or lower at 12 months, without repeat prolapse surgery or pessary treatment
results.note: Complementary overall recurrence was 20/32 (62.5%) versus 23/33 (69.7%), P=.45. Table 2 reports randomized-arm denominators; five mesh patients were censored from the 12-month evaluation, including three reoperated for prolapse.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 86.e3–86.e5

results.note: Patients reoperated for prolapse were excluded from this subjective analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Patient satisfaction and QOL, p 86.e4; Table 2

results.measure: Anterior wall POP-Q stage 2 or higher at approximately 12 months
results.note: The paper designates compartment-specific cure as secondary; the tabulated anterior recurrence proportions did not differ significantly.

harms.label: Mesh exposure
harms.note: Three exposures required operating-room mesh excision; two persisted asymptomatically at one year.

harms.label: Reoperation for prolapse or mesh exposure
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Complications, pp 86.e5–86.e6
harms.note: P=.017; three prolapse and three exposure reoperations involved five patients because one underwent both. One patient also underwent sling revision for persistent voiding dysfunction.

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent prolapse
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Objective recurrence, pp 86.e4–86.e5
harms.note: P=.11; two sacral colpopexies and one iliococcygeal suspension.

harms.label: Apical Gore-Tex suture exposure
harms.note: Two control patients required office suture removal.

delivery.label: Mesh and apical suspension technique
delivery.value: Six fellowship-trained surgeons used anterior or total Prolift mesh; the no-mesh arm used uterosacral or sacrospinous suspension. Each surgeon had performed more than 30 vaginal colpopexies and at least 10 Prolift procedures before enrollment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Surgery, p 86.e2

delivery.label: Operative time
delivery.note: P=.53; concomitant posterior repair was more common without mesh (82% versus 56%, P=.026).

reports.label: Three-year final analysis
reports.citation: Gutman RE, Nosti PA, Sokol AI, et al. "Three-year outcomes of vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2013;122(4):770-777. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3182a49dac
reports.followUp: Three-year questionnaires; blinded POP-Q examination at two or three years
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, p 771; Results, p 772

results.measure: POP-Q stage 1 or lower, no bulge symptoms, Patient Global Impression of Improvement much or very much better, and no repeat prolapse surgery or pessary; complete-case analysis
results.note: Three mesh recipients reoperated for recurrent prolapse were failures for composite cure; reoperated participants were excluded from anatomic and subjective analyses.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 771; Table 2, p 775

results.note: Within-group improvement from baseline (P<.01); between-group POP-Q stage did not differ at final examination.

results.endpoint: Three-year anatomic cure, POP-Q stage 1 or lower
results.measure: Overall POP-Q stage 1 or lower at 2- or 3-year blinded examination; complete cases excluding prolapse reoperations
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 771; Table 2, p 775

results.measure: No prolapse beyond hymen (Ba, Bp and C at or proximal to 0) at 2- or 3-year blinded examination; complete cases
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 771; Table 2, p 775

results.measure: Absence of patient-reported bulge at 3 years; questionnaire complete cases
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 771; Table 2, p 775

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent prolapse
harms.locator: Full text, Results, pp 772–774; Table 2, p 775
harms.note: All three prolapse reoperations were in mesh recipients; one had urinary retention and voiding dysfunction at 4.5 months and underwent another prolapse operation at 17.5 months.

harms.label: Mesh exposure through three years
harms.note: A small asymptomatic exposure at the three-year visit occurred at a previously excised location; paper reports five total recipients with exposure.

harms.label: De novo dyspareunia and stress urinary incontinence at three years
harms.note: The report gives event counts but does not state at-risk denominators for these incident symptoms.

delivery.label: Three-year follow-up ascertainment
delivery.value: Three-year quality-of-life questionnaires: 51/65 (78%; 25 mesh, 26 no mesh); blinded POP-Q examinations at two or three years: 41/65 (63%; 20 mesh, 21 no mesh); median follow-up 3.05 years (IQR 2.97–3.15).
